title: Rehearsal traffic fabric with epochal rewind for reproducible canaries
author: Evelyn Tran
release_notes: Adds a rehearsal traffic fabric and epochal rewind tooling to capture deterministic cohort snapshots for reproducible canaries; includes observability hooks and a lightweight replay harness for on-demand root-cause analysis.

description:
Motivation: Reproducing flaky regressions found during canary/A-B promotes is expensive. Teams need a deterministic way to capture and replay the exact cohort traffic used in a canary so debugging and postmortems are reliable. This PR introduces a small-footprint rehearsal traffic fabric and an "epochal rewind" snapshotter that together enable reproducible canaries, deterministic rollbacks, and on-demand replay for root cause analysis.

What this does (high level):
- Rehearsal traffic fabric: an in-process router that can shadow or rehearse traffic into isolated rehearsal lanes without impacting production routing. Supports fractional mirroring, session-affinity preservation, and lane-level quotas.
- Epochal snapshotter: captures a compact, deterministic snapshot for a cohort (user/session markers + normalized request events + metadata) at commit points. Snapshots are immutable epochs that can be pinned to a rollout.
- Rewind & replay harness: lightweight replay path that consumes an epoch, replays requests to a target model variant in a sandboxed lane, and emits parity diffs and telemetry. Designed to be low-cost and deterministic (time-normalization and KV-barriers).
- Telemetry and tie-ins: cohort markers, replay traces, and smoke assertions wired into Console and the rollouts API so a user can pin an epoch to a canary and run a replay from the web UI or CLI.

Design notes and constraints:
- Determinism: we avoid capturing external side-effects; the snapshotter records a normalized event stream and requires optional flush hooks for services with mutating side-effects. See docs/rehearsal-playbook.md for integration points.
- Storage: epochs are stored as append-only blobs with compact metadata index to support quick lookups and retention policies. Backing store is pluggable; this change adds a local S3-backed implementation.
- Safety: rehearsal lanes are opt-in behind "rehearsal.enabled" and require RBAC to execute replays in private deployments. Replays run in a sandbox and cannot mutate production caches by default.

Checklist: 
- [x] Fabric router and rehearsal lanes implemented
- [x] Epochal snapshot schema + store implementation
- [x] Replay harness with deterministic time-normalization
- [x] Telemetry markers and Console hooks
- [x] Feature flag + RBAC gating
- [x] Unit and integration tests (local)
- [x] Docs and playbook added

Commits summary: a1f3d9c adds the snapshotter and storage schema; b4c7e2f implements router and API routes; d2e9b11 wires telemetry markers; f6a2c38 adds the deterministic replay harness and tests; e8b7f55 author docs and playbook.

Files changed (high level): rollouts/rehearsal/fabric.go handles lane lifecycle and traffic mirroring; rollouts/snapshot/epochal_store.go defines snapshot format, flush hooks and S3 store; telemetry/cohort_markers.go adds markers tied to request lifecycle; simulators/replay/harness.py is the python harness for reproducible replays used in CI and by the debugging CLI; api/routes/rehearsal_routes.go exposes endpoints for creating epochs, listing, and triggering replays; docs/rehearsal-playbook.md describes integration patterns and known caveats.

Review convo highlights:
- Determinism concerns: added a KV-cache barrier and optional flush hook to ensure consistent snapshots.
- Time drift in replay: time-normalization added to harness and a long-session test to detect drift.
- Security gating: feature flag + RBAC checks added so private deployments keep control.

CI: Initial run had two flaky tests in the replay harness (time normalization mismatch) which failed on linux-ktest; I pushed a patch to normalize epoch timestamps and re-ran. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, e2e smoke profile).

How to use: See docs/rehearsal-playbook.md for the step-by-step guide. Quick flow: 1) create a rehearsal lane and enable rehearsal.enabled; 2) pin an epoch to a canary promote; 3) trigger a replay to the candidate variant in sandbox; 4) review parity diffs and telemetry in Console; 5) optionally promote epoch or rollback using the replay evidence.

Backward compatibility and rollout: This is fully backward compatible; rehearsal routes are opt-in. Storage schema includes a migration path for existing snapshot artifacts (migration is additive). Retention defaults are conservative (30d) and configurable per workspace.

Operational notes: Replays can be expensive for long epochs — the playbook recommends limiting epoch size and using sampling for long-running sessions. The retention policy and compact metadata index keep list operations fast.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals from Priya, Carlos and Samir. Merge commit: 7c3b1e4.

Related: ENG-7842 implements higher-level rollout integration planned for Q1; PM-1921 tracks UX work for pinning epochs in Console.
